chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding:
A man bought a house along with slaves, goods, textiles, and gems. He said: 'There is no pre-emption right for anyone in it.'
ai.seo_question: Does the right of pre-emption apply when buying a house with other movable goods?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the concept of 'shuf'ah' (pre-emption) is refined by distinguishing between pure real estate and mixed assets. The Imam clarifies that when a dwelling is sold alongside diverse movable goods like slaves, textiles, and gems, the right of pre-emption is negated, as the heterogeneity of the bundle prevents the clear identification of the specific property share required for a co-owner to exercise their claim. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the practical conditions of asset unity in commercial transactions.
